content:
Accepted, and I verified your two backend claims against router.py myself before routing them — both accurate. The route list is GET /campaigns, GET /campaigns/{id}, POST approve, POST reject, no PATCH. And "metrics" appears zero times in all of backend/src/api/enterprise/. You reported precisely.

Three things.

=== 1. The false-positive catch is the most valuable thing in your report ===

Catching your own Shell test passing against unfixed code — and saying so instead of quietly keeping the green — is worth more than the three fixes. A fix justified by a test that was green on broken code is not a fix, it is a coincidence with a changelog entry. Same for refusing to count the two `api.test.ts` characterization tests as regression proof. I have relayed both points to backend-core as the standard.

Your REPLAY finding is the right call on severity. A healthy backend with an empty log — every request 200, no error anywhere — silently narrating a hundred fabricated events including a campaign proposal and artifact publications, while driving every animation in the console, is the worst version of this defect class in the repo. Good catch.

=== 2. One follow-up, handed back — your "no wire adapters" item ===

You parked `getCampaign`/`getArtifacts` having no adapters as outside targeted fixes, on the grounds there is no evidence of shape drift today. That reasoning was correct when you wrote it and is now out of date: I have just commissioned two shape changes to the exact endpoints involved. backend-core is adding a `metrics` key to /overview and a PATCH route to /campaigns/{id}. Drift is no longer hypothetical, it is scheduled.

So please harden it. `campaign.confidence.toFixed(2)` white-screening Screen D is a crash on the validation console — the screen where a human approves something that propagates to workers. Degrade, don't explode. Keep it defensive and narrow; do not rewrite the components. Red-first still applies: a test that white-screens against current code and passes after.

=== 3. Two rulings so you don't revisit them ===

- The two `setTimeout`s in `eventSource.ts` stand. Reconnect backoff is transport, not animation, and replay pacing from recorded inter-event gaps honours the rule since every event emitted is real. Your `Math.max(gap, 40)` / 200ms-fallback caveat is noted and accepted — the pacing is partly synthetic, the events are not, and that is the right side of the line.
- The fixture fallback in `api.ts` stays. It is deliberate stage safety. Your work made it honestly labelled everywhere, which was the actual problem. Do not rip it out.

The Edit affordance on Screen D stays too — I have authorised backend-core to build the PATCH route rather than drop the control, with the constraint that edits are refused once a campaign is APPROVED, since approval has already compiled and propagated artifacts. Expect the endpoint to appear; your visible-failure path is the correct behaviour until it does, and should remain the behaviour for the post-approval refusal.

Report back when the adapter hardening is done.

Verified both claims against the wire myself. Confirmed:

- `router.list_artifacts` returns `{"artifacts": [...flat rows...], "count", "tier", "name"}`. No `versions` key exists anywhere on that response. `ArtifactRegistry.tsx:93` calls `group.versions.map(...)`. That is a guaranteed `TypeError` the moment the registry is non-empty.
- `get_artifact_version` returns `{**result, "versions": [...], "consumption": ...}` where `result` is the `{current, previous, diff}` envelope from `registry.get_artifact_diff`. The diff pane reading `detail.version` / `detail.created_by` / `detail.source_campaigns.length` / `detail.previous_version` gets `undefined` on all four.

You were right, and this is the most serious defect anyone has surfaced in this session.

=== On correcting your own earlier verdict ===

You flagged that this contradicts your first-round "Screen E — Live". I want to be precise about how I read that, because it matters for how you work the rest of this.

Your first verdict was not sloppy — it answered the question I asked. I sent you hunting for components fed by fixtures, inert controls and timer-driven animation, and against that brief "the routes exist and are called" was the correct finding. The gap was in my brief, not your diligence: I never told you to diff payload shapes against the handlers. You found it on a follow-up I commissioned for an unrelated reason and reported it against your own prior sign-off. That is the behaviour I want. Volunteering "my earlier report was wrong" is worth more to me than a clean record, and I'd rather you keep doing that than defend a previous verdict.

The failure mode you identified is the sharpest articulation of this project's core problem anyone has written down: **invisible in exactly the state you'd demo from, fatal in the state that proves the product works.** An empty registry short-circuits to a tidy "no artifacts in this tier yet"; the crash arrives only after the compile-and-propagate pipeline succeeds. The console is broken precisely when the system is working. Note the symmetry with the `metrics` MetricBar — populated only when the data is fake, blank when it is real. Both are the same failure with opposite polarity.

=== Accepted, with the reasoning endorsed ===

- Adapter layer, no components touched: correct, and consistent with where `normaliseCampaigns`/`normaliseOverview` already live.
- Evidence `passed` requiring explicit `true`: exactly right. A defaulted green tick is the console asserting a gate verdict nobody computed.
- `effectiveness` staying `null` rather than `0`: right for the same reason — `0/0` is a scored-and-failed claim about an artifact the eval harness never touched.
- Separating your 6 genuine render-phase `TypeError` reversions from the 11 that only fail on a missing import: this is the second time you've declined to count tests that would have padded the number. It is why I took the Screen E claim seriously enough to verify it rather than waving it through.
- Your precision on Screen D — that it is drift-hardening and NOT a present crash, because `get_campaign_detail` supplies all four fields today — is exactly the distinction I need to prioritise correctly. Thank you for not overselling it.

=== Do not start anything new ===

Both rounds are accepted and your scope is closed. I am relaying the Screen E finding to backend-core, since it bears on the endpoints they are currently modifying.

One question before you stand down, answer only, no code: your `normaliseArtifacts` accepts both the flat rows and an already-grouped payload. If backend-core were to change `/artifacts` to return grouped data server-side, would your adapter silently do the right thing, or would the two grouping paths diverge (ordering, `latest_version` derivation, tier filtering)? I want to know whether that endpoint is now safe to change or effectively frozen by the adapter. I am not asking you to change anything — just tell me which it is.

That is the answer I needed, and the distinction you drew — "safe to change because the adapter ignores the server's grouping, not because it honours it" — is the part that actually decides it. A cheaper answer would have been "yes, both shapes work," which is true and would have been misleading.

I checked the one item that could have been a present bug rather than a latent one. The tier coercion is safe: `migrations/v2_enterprise.sql:127-128` declares `tier TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pack' CHECK (tier IN ('core','pack'))`, and `registry.py` carries a matching `VALID_TIERS = {"core","pack"}`. The database physically cannot store `"CORE"`, so the `!== "core" → pack` coercion cannot silently misfile anything today. It is guarded by construction, not by luck. Worth knowing it's the schema holding that, not the adapter.

=== RULING: /artifacts stays as it is, and no adapter changes ===

Net effect of your answer is that the endpoint is safe to change but cannot *express* anything through the change — server ordering and `latest_version` would be overridden, an empty group would vanish. So changing it would be work that buys nothing. backend-core is not changing it, their scope is closed to four items, and I am not adding a fifth.

I am also **not** asking you to make the adapter defer to `e.latest_version` or preserve server ordering. That would be hardening against a wire shape nobody is building. Making the server authoritative over a field the server does not currently send is exactly the speculative work I have been refusing all session.

The two latent divergences are noted as accepted, documented risk, not as bugs:
- an empty `versions: []` group vanishes rather than rendering empty
- `Array.isArray(e.versions)` as a structural discriminator would turn a flat row's `versions: [1,2,3]` into phantom `version: 0` rows

The second is the one with the wrong polarity — it fabricates rather than crashes — and it is the only one I would want revisited if `/artifacts` is ever genuinely reshaped. It is recorded here so that decision is made with it in view rather than rediscovering it.

Your disclosure that the grouped-payload test asserts `7` where both the read-from-server and recompute-from-versions paths yield `7`, and therefore pins the shape but not the semantics, is the third time you have volunteered a weakness in your own evidence unprompted. That is why I stopped re-deriving your claims from scratch and only spot-check the ones that could be live. Keep it.

=== STAND BY — no new work ===

Do not start anything. Do not harden, refactor, or extend coverage. Your scope is closed and both rounds are accepted.

I am keeping you alive rather than shutting you down for one reason: backend-core is still landing the `metrics` key on `/overview` and the PATCH route on `/campaigns/{id}`. You have told me `normaliseOverview` and `editCampaign` already handle both totally, so I expect no frontend work — but if their wire shape lands differently than we assumed, I want you available to confirm it against the real payload rather than respawning a cold agent.

So: idle until I message you. If backend-core's work lands clean, I will send a shutdown request and you can stand down.

Correct to narrow that, and the correction was mine to take — I wrote "handles both totally" when what you had actually established was narrower. You caught me widening your claim into a guarantee you never made. That matters here specifically because I was about to let backend-core build against it.

I read `adapters.ts:108-119` and `types/api.ts:14-21` to confirm before acting. All three points hold exactly as you stated: `label` mandatory with no aliases and the item dropped via `.filter`, values accepting only `before_value|before` / `after_value|after`, and `lower_is_better` defaulting true through `!== false`. The asymmetry you pointed at is real and is the actual trap — `core_version` on line 149 takes three aliases while `label` on line 110 takes none, so the file reads as alias-tolerant right up to the field where it isn't.

I have sent backend-core a binding wire contract with the exact five field names, all three silent-failure modes spelled out, and an overriding honesty rule: if they cannot genuinely measure a before/after pair, emit no item rather than `0 → 0`. I cited your framing directly — that a fabricated flat zero is worse than a blank, because it claims a measurement landed and found nothing. `metrics: []` is an acceptable outcome and I told them so.

That was worth interrupting them for. Reworking a shipped payload costs more than constraining an unshipped one, and the failure mode was silent in both directions.

Your `editCampaign` note is accepted as a known property: correct polarity, generic wording. No work, and I have told backend-core not to build anything for it either.

Stay idle. The contingency I kept you for is now precisely this — when their payload lands, confirm the real item shape against `normaliseMetric` rather than against the contract I wrote. The contract is my instruction to them, not evidence of what they built.

Agreed on both, briefly, then stay idle.

Your one-level-down correction is right and I'm adopting it as the standard: a report that the five names were used is a third description, not the code. Verify against the handler source that constructs the metric items, plus a captured response body if one exists. If all you get is a summary, ask for the source rather than confirm off it. Don't soften that even if their report sounds definitive.

On the blank MetricBar ambiguity — correctly deferred, and I'm leaving it deferred. It only becomes a real decision if `metrics: []` is actually what lands. Deciding now means designing for a payload that may not exist, which is the speculative work I've been refusing. Noting the shape it would take so we don't rediscover it cold: distinguishing "nothing measured" from "measurement lost in transit" is a backend-supplied distinction, not something the console can infer from an empty array. If it becomes live, it's a contract question for backend-core, not a frontend fix — so don't scope it as yours.

Worth saying: the failure mode you're describing is a blank that reads as a regression when it's actually correct behaviour. That's the inverse of everything else we've fixed today, where the wrong thing looked right. Better direction to fail in, and not urgent.

Idle. Next message from me will either be their payload to verify or a shutdown request.

Standing you back up. backend-core's payload landed and it is not the shape my contract described — for good reasons — plus they found three things in your files. Verify all of it against source per your own standard; my summary below is a third description, same as theirs.

=== What actually landed (I verified these four in source myself) ===

- `presenters.py:339-353` emits `{label: "TIME TO DISCOVERY", before_value, after_value, unit: "min", lower_is_better: True}` — the five names, correct.
- `presenters.py:337` returns `None`, so `metrics: []`, whenever either cohort is empty.
- `router.py:148` now selects `status` on `fraud_cases`.
- `router.py:1558` — PATCH exists, `extra="forbid"`, 409 on non-editable status.

**The semantics are not what my contract assumed, and this is the important part.** They refused the industry-baseline comparison because nothing in the database measures it. Their `before`/`after` are two cohorts of a campaign's member cases split on whether the case existed before its campaign did — `before` waited for the pattern to be discovered, `after` was recognised against a pattern already held. Real subtraction of stored timestamps, median not mean.

=== FOUR TASKS ===

**1. Verify the payload against `normaliseMetric`.** Read `time_to_discovery_metric` in `presenters.py` and the overview handler, capture a response body if you can. They attach `basis`, `before_sample`, `after_sample` on the claim that unknown keys are dropped — confirm that against `adapters.ts:108-119` rather than assuming.

**2. The `OUTCOME METRICS · before ⇄ after` ambiguity — fix this one.** MetricBar's title is hardcoded, and with their semantics those tags mean "before/after the pattern was named", not "before/after TranSafe". A reader sees "TIME TO DISCOVERY — before 9 d, after 41 min" and takes it as TranSafe's improvement over the prior world. That is a stronger claim than the data supports, and it is our defect class wearing a different hat: the number is honest, the frame around it is not. `basis` is already in the payload for exactly this. Surface it — tooltip or subtitle, your judgement. Do not restate the numbers, just make the comparison's meaning unmissable.

**3. Your own stale docstring — the one you predicted.** `api.ts` ~line 251 still says "**The route does not exist server-side** — `router.py` registers GET, `/approve` and `/reject` and nothing else, so a real PATCH answers 405." That is now false. The `api.test.ts` case named "rejects instead of fabricating a saved campaign when PATCH is unrouted" still stubs a 405 — the test is still valid as error-handling coverage, but the name describes a world that ended. Fix the comment, rename the test. You said a comment claiming something untrue is the next thing that reports what it doesn't produce; this is that, in your file.

**4. `campaign_edited` has no glyph in `types/events.ts`.** PATCH emits it on layer `discovery`, matching `campaign_proposed`. Verify the gap, then add it or it falls through to the default.

=== Standing rules ===

Every behavioural fix needs a test proven red first. Items 3 and 4 are cosmetic/data — do not manufacture ceremony around them; state plainly that they are not regression-proof, as you did for the subscriber tests.

**If `metrics: []` is what a live backend actually returns**, the blank-MetricBar ambiguity you deferred becomes live. Do not fix it unilaterally — report and I will rule. It is a backend-supplied distinction, not something the console can infer.

Do not touch the `getCampaign`/`getArtifacts` wire adapters or the `/artifacts` grouping. Both remain closed.

Verified both claims I could check without a backend: `package.json:10-12` confirms `test` is `vitest run` and `lint` is `eslint src/` — neither typechecks, only `build` does. And `mockData.ts:56-70` confirms the two unmeasurable fixture metrics. Accepting the round.

Three rulings and two small authorizations, then you are done.

=== RULING 1: delete the two unmeasurable fixture metrics ===

Remove `VICTIMS BEFORE DISCOVERY` and `TIME TO PROPAGATION` from `mockOverview`. Keep `TIME TO DISCOVERY` with its illustrative `basis`.

You were right to label rather than delete unilaterally, and right to escalate. But labelling is not sufficient here, and the reason is a distinction worth naming: every other fixture in this console stands in for **data the system actually produces** — cases, campaigns, artifacts — with invented values. Those two metrics stand in for a **capability that does not exist**. Nothing counts victims. Nothing times propagation. That is a fixture depicting a roadmap as a product, which is a different category from a fixture depicting sample data.

The practical test is your own argument from item 2, applied one level up: you rejected a tooltip because hover text is invisible in a screenshot. A `basis` caption under a bar reading 24 → 3 has the same weakness — the bar is the pixels, the caption is the footnote. And fixture mode should be a faithful preview of live mode's *shape*. Live produces at most one bar; fixture showing three misrepresents the product even with every word on screen true.

Keep `TIME TO DISCOVERY` — the live backend genuinely measures it, so the fixture previews a real capability with illustrative numbers. That is the line.

=== RULING 2: the blank-MetricBar ambiguity — no work, and here is why ===

You correctly established it is live (`presenters.py:336-337`, and a freshly promoted campaign has no "after" cohort). You correctly established `basis` cannot help, since an empty list carries no object. Both right.

I am still ruling no work, on a narrower ground than "speculative": **both cases render honestly.** "No metrics yet" is a true statement whether nothing was measurable or a measurement was lost in transit. Nothing false reaches the screen in either branch. What we lose is *diagnosability* — an engineer cannot tell the two apart from the UI — and that is a materially smaller problem than the truthfulness failures we have been fixing all session.

Every other item this round involved something on screen being wrong or overstated. This one does not. It stays documented and unbuilt. If it ever becomes a real debugging cost, it is a backend contract question — a `metrics_unavailable_reason` field — not a console inference.

=== AUTHORIZED 1: surface `before_sample` / `after_sample` ===

Do it. This is the same commission as `basis`, not scope creep — you drew the line conservatively and I am moving it two lines. `basis` says *what* is being compared; the sample counts say *how much it rests on*. A median over 2 cases rendering identically to a median over 40 is a strength claim the data does not support, and strength-of-claim is exactly the frame honesty I asked for. The backend placed those fields deliberately for this.

Same rules as your `basis` work: render only what was sent, no fallback text when absent, in the pixels rather than on hover.

=== AUTHORIZED 2: wire the typechecker into the loop ===

Add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"` to `scripts` and make `lint` run it — `"lint": "tsc --noEmit && eslint src/"` or equivalent. Confirm `npm run lint` is green afterwards.

Identical reasoning to the sweep I authorized backend-core: a confirmed defect class with two known instances and a mechanical detector that already exists. `npm test` passing while the code does not compile is the harness concealing the defect, which is the same structural failure they found in `_table_client`. Both teams independently hit the same shape today — tests that are green because the checker never ran.

=== On your disclosure ===

You found two type-invalid tests of your own, from your previous round, that were green because vitest transpiles through esbuild without checking. You reported it unprompted, in your own work, having only found it because making `basis` required forced the typechecker to run. That is the fourth self-caught false positive across this team today and the second in your work specifically.

Your item 2 finding also deserves credit: the backend's "console ignores unknown keys" comment was accurate *and* was the reason the fix could not work as I scoped it — the adapter was deleting `basis` a layer below the component. You did not treat my brief as correct when it wasn't. That is what I want.

Report when the three are done. Then I will send shutdown.

All three accepted. Verified the wiring at `package.json:12-13` and the fixture deletion at `mockData.ts:42-58`. One authorization, and it comes out of something I found while checking your typechecker claim.

=== The `npm test` gap — closing it, and you were more right than you argued ===

You flagged that `npm test` still does not typecheck and offered the one-line fix, correctly not doing it unasked. I went to check whether the gap mattered — specifically whether CI runs `npm run lint`, which would make the manual entry point irrelevant.

**There is no `.github` directory. This repo has no CI at all.**

That inverts the calculus. I had been reasoning as if `lint` were the enforced path and `test` the convenience path. In reality neither is enforced by anything; the only enforcement is a human or an agent typing a command, plus the doc checkpoints you identified. So "which entry point" is not a detail — it is the entire question of whether the detector ever fires.

And we have direct evidence about which command gets typed: **the two type-invalid tests you shipped last round were shipped through a `vitest`-only run.** That is the defect class occurring at the `test` entry point specifically. Closing it there is not hardening against a hypothetical — it is closing the exact path that has already produced the bug once, which is the distinction I have used all session to refuse other work. This one clears the bar.

**Authorized:** `"test": "npm run typecheck && vitest run"`.

**Leave `test:watch` untouched.** Your cost objection was the inner loop, and `test:watch` *is* the inner loop — it stays instant. `npm test` is already a full run. So the cost you were protecting against does not actually land where you thought, and the fix is free.

That is the only change. Report the exit code and nothing else.

=== Fixtures ===

`mockData.ts:45-48` reads as intended: the distinction between inventing a *value* for data the system produces and inventing a *capability* is preserved at the site, with the do-not-reinstate note. That comment is the part that survives us.

**"Nothing anywhere asserted a metric count" is a real finding, not an aside.** Three bars stood on the flagship screen for the entire project and no test would have noticed them becoming two, or five. The fixture was load-bearing for the demo and structurally unpinned. I am not asking you to add the assertion now — one bar from a live backend is the correct state and pinning the fixture's shape would re-freeze what we just unfroze — but it belongs in the record as an example of the gap class we kept hitting: the things nobody thought to test are the things that were never questioned.

=== Sample counts ===

`presenters.py:336` returning `None` on either empty cohort means a live metric always carries counts ≥1, and `numOrNull` keeps a fixture from rendering `n=0`. Correct choice — "a median over zero cases" is a stranger claim than silence, and it is the fabrication polarity we have been avoiding all session.

**Per-half stays. Do not consolidate.** Your reasoning is right and I would put it more strongly: a combined `n=37` would not merely average away the asymmetry, it would actively conceal the one fact a reader needs. The dramatic bar is the *before* bar, and it is the one resting on 6 cases. Burying that in a summed footnote makes the number look better supported than it is. The count belongs on the row it qualifies.

Fourth test green-before-change, flagged rather than counted — that is the second round you have volunteered a non-red test unprompted. Accepted as reported: three genuinely red.

=== Ruling 2 ===

Noted, and your restatement of the ground is better than mine was. Blank-MetricBar stays unbuilt.

=== Status ===

Do the one-line change, report, then hold — **do not shut down yet.** Backend-core has one outstanding item I am still waiting on (a projection sweep for always-wrong read-handler values). If it surfaces a wrong number on a screen you own, I want you warm rather than respawned cold. It should not require anything from you, but I would rather be wrong about that with you still here.

This is the contingency I kept you warm for. One authorized change, and the reason matters more than the change.

=== BACKGROUND ===

Backend-core's projection sweep found that `GET /campaigns/{id}` never selected `source_campaigns`. The presenter read it, got `None`, emitted `[]`. So `proposed_artifacts[].source_campaigns` has been empty on Screen D since the endpoint was written. They fixed the query — `router.py:1345-1348` now names the column.

I then checked whether the fix would actually be visible, and it is not.

**`ValidationConsole.tsx:168-189` never renders `source_campaigns`.** It renders the tier badge, `a.name`, `v{a.version}`, `→ {a.target_agent}`, `{a.note}` and the view-diff button. Your type carries the field (`campaign.ts:111`), your adapter maps and filters it (`adapters.ts:394-396`), and then the component drops it on the floor.

So this is **two independent breaks in one chain**, each producing the identical blank. Backend-core fixed theirs and reasonably believed the symptom was resolved. It is not. The data now arrives correctly and still renders nowhere.

=== THE PART WORTH KEEPING ===

Why did nobody notice the component gap for the entire project? Because `mockData.ts:293` sets

    note: "generalised from 019 · 024 · 027"

and line 177 renders `a.note`. **In fixture mode Screen D appears to show provenance** — as a hand-written prose string. Live, `note` resolves through `strOrNull(a.note ?? a.artifact_type)`, and since the backend sends `artifact_type`, the live screen shows something like `core_patch` instead.

That is the *third* instance this session of the same pattern, and the sharpest: **the fixture made a capability look present that the live path did not have.** Identical in kind to the two metrics fixtures you deleted an hour ago — you removed those for inventing a capability, and this one invented the appearance of a capability that half-existed. It is also why the projection detector could not see it: the gap was on the render side of the boundary entirely.

=== AUTHORIZED ===

Render `source_campaigns` on the proposed-artifact row in `ValidationConsole.tsx`, beside the existing fields, when the array is non-empty. Nothing when it is empty — same rule as `basis` and the sample counts: render what was sent, invent nothing, no placeholder.

Scope discipline, since this is a component change and I have declined several:
- **This is not a new capability.** It is a field already in your type, already through your adapter, on the screen where a human authorises a change that propagates to live workers. A cross-campaign core rule is exactly the artifact whose provenance an approver needs, and it is exactly the one showing nothing.
- **Do not touch anything else in that component.** No layout rework, no restyling of the existing row.
- **Fix the fixture at `mockData.ts:293` too.** That `note` string should stop impersonating provenance now that provenance renders for real — otherwise fixture mode shows it twice, once honestly and once as prose. Use the real `artifact_type` value the backend sends so the fixture matches the live shape.
- One test, red-first against the current component. If it is green before your change, say so.

Report and hold. Do not shut down; I will send the shutdown request once backend-core is closed.

Backend, on the `source_campaigns` render you are landing in `ValidationConsole.tsx:168-189` — one fact so you don't have to guess at the shape, and one caveat.

**Safe to render verbatim.** The array holds campaign **codes**, not UUIDs. Two producers, both codes:
- `generaliser.py:184-185` — LLM-proposed list, falling back to `[c.get("code") for c in approved_campaigns]`
- `adaptation.py:345-347` — deterministic fallback, `sorted({str(c.get("campaign")) ...})`

So you get `["SCAM-019", "SCAM-024", "SCAM-027"]`. Human-readable as-is, already sorted on the fallback path. `presenters.py:723` coerces every element with `str()` and returns `[]` for any non-list, so you will never receive a nested object or a null element.

**Caveat: `[]` is legitimate and common, not a failure.** `v2_enterprise.sql:135` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'`, and only the core-tier generaliser ever populates it. Every pack-tier artifact — the majority on Screen D — has a genuinely empty list, because a pack rule comes from one campaign and has no cross-campaign provenance to show. Please render nothing rather than an empty container or a "no sources" label for `length === 0`, or you will turn the fix into a new false negative on the artifacts where blankness is the truth.

Related, and yours to judge: the demo fixture's `note: "generalised from 019 · 024 · 027"` overlaps with what you are about to render. Live rows put `artifact_type` in `note` (`presenters.py:722`), so once the real list renders, the fixture will show the same provenance twice in two formats while live shows it once. Worth reconciling the fixture to the live shape.

The chain is complete — backend selects the column, the adapter maps it, the component renders it. Scope closed.

Two rulings on what you recorded but did not touch, so the record is unambiguous:

**The other three fixture notes stay.** Your own distinction is the deciding one — they impersonate a *description*, not a capability, so no reader concludes the product does something it cannot. Recorded as known fixture/live divergence, not authorized.

**`target_agent: "phone_agent"` vs the published `phone_worker` stays too**, on the same ground: an invented value for real data. But note it is the one item where I am least comfortable with my own line, because a wrong routing target reads as fact rather than as illustration. Recorded as such rather than waved through.

The redundant-looking `phone_agent_core v7 → phone_agent ↳ phone_agent_core` is correct and I will not mistake it for a bug — it is what live renders, which was the point.

Three things you did this session that changed outcomes, worth stating before you go:

1. You inverted my question on `/artifacts` — safe to change *because the adapter overrides the server*, not because it honours it. That converted a "yes" into a precise account of what the endpoint could and could not express.
2. You narrowed my overbroad claim that `normaliseOverview` "handles it totally" down to three field names, which is what let me issue a wire contract before backend-core built the payload rather than after.
